newsitem.title: CHINA: China to strengthen military exchanges with Burma.
newsitem.headline: China to strengthen military exchanges with Burma.

text.p: China's Premier Li Peng has said military exchanges with Burma should be strengthened to improve bilateral ties, the official People's Daily said on Saturday.

"Strengthening Sino-Burmese military exchanges is conducive to promoting the overall development of friendly cooperative relations between the two countries," Li told visiting Burmese General Maung Aye on Friday. He did not elaborate.
Maung Aye is vice chairman of Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council.
Li reiterated that China was against foreign interference in the domestic affairs of any country, the newspaper said.
Both China and Burma have been criticised by Western countries for their human rights record.
Li also slammed Western countries for spreading the theory that China was a threat to the world. He said the theory was baseless.
In a separate meeting with Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian, Maung Aye said he hoped friendly cooperative relations between the two would be enhanced, the Xinhua news agency said.
Chi told Maung Aye that China attached great importance to cooperation between the two armies, Xinhua said. It gave no further details.
